messages:
Marcus Reed: heads up: found a starvation edge case in two-queue policy under sustained short traffic. long queue can get effectively stuck if short arrivals keep the short queue non-empty and aging doesn’t trip.

Marcus Reed: repro from load test (mixed 95/5, but 95% short steady + long trickle). after ~6-8 min, long requests start piling up; a few never get dispatched (wait > 120s) even though decode is making progress on shorts.

Marcus Reed: env:
- runtime: runtime-1.18.0-rc3
- policy: two_queue_v1
- config:
  - short_long_threshold_tokens=384
  - short_bias=0.85
  - long_min_share=0.00 (default)
  - aging_ms=1500
  - max_skew=12
- model: llama-3-70b-instruct
- sku: H100-80G x8

loadtest-bot: Load test run finished: mixed_scheduler_starvation_2026-02-05T19:12Z
Artifacts: s3://redwood-loadtests/runtime/mixed_scheduler_starvation_2026-02-05T19-12Z/
Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rt-scheduler/mixed?var-run=mixed_scheduler_starvation_2026-02-05T19-12Z

Marcus Reed: quick symptoms:
- scheduler.long.queue_depth climbs to 70+ and stays elevated
- scheduler.long.time_in_queue_p95 keeps increasing (peaks ~98s)
- scheduler.starvation_counter{class="long"} increments, but dispatch_share{class="long"} stays near 0%

Marcus Reed: excerpt from scheduler debug logs (enabled `RUNTIME_SCHED_DEBUG=1`):
```
I0205 19:22:14.901Z sched: iter=18421 short_q=43 long_q=19 choose=short reason=short_nonempty bias=0.85 long_age_ms_p95=6123
I0205 19:22:14.908Z sched: iter=18422 short_q=45 long_q=20 choose=short reason=short_nonempty bias=0.85 long_age_ms_p95=6882
I0205 19:22:14.915Z sched: iter=18423 short_q=42 long_q=20 choose=short reason=short_nonempty bias=0.85 long_age_ms_p95=7449
I0205 19:22:14.921Z sched: iter=18424 short_q=44 long_q=21 choose=short reason=short_nonempty bias=0.85 long_age_ms_p95=8031
I0205 19:22:14.929Z sched: iter=18425 short_q=46 long_q=23 choose=short reason=short_nonempty bias=0.85 long_age_ms_p95=8610
...
I0205 19:22:31.004Z sched: iter=18592 short_q=51 long_q=31 choose=short reason=short_nonempty bias=0.85 long_age_ms_p95=24118
```

Lena Fischer: :eyes: wait why isn’t aging triggering? long_age_ms_p95 is >> aging_ms=1500. We should be flipping to long when the head has aged past threshold.

Marcus Reed: yeah. I dug a bit: we’re computing “effective age” off `req.last_enqueued_ts` but we update that on every prefill->decode transition (and also when we “rehydrate” from waiting_for_kv). for long prompts, they bounce through a couple states before entering the long decode queue, so the age keeps getting reset.

Omar El-Sayed: that tracks w/ the prefill/decode separation hook PR (24857). we enqueue a decode work item after prefill completes; its enqueue_ts is new.

Julian Moore: do we have per-state metrics for this? (prefill done -> decode enqueue delay vs actual time-in-system)

Marcus Reed: not directly. current metric is `time_in_queue_ms` per class which uses the queue’s enqueue time (so it looks fine-ish until it isn’t). but in logs you can see long_age_ms_p95 is computed differently, and it’s using the “work item enqueue” timestamp.

Sofia Ivanova: can you share a concrete example req timeline? want to ensure we’re not mixing “time waiting for batch slot” vs “time alive in system”.

Marcus Reed: yep. one long req in the trace:
- t0: accepted
- t0+3ms: put into prefill lane
- t0+280ms: prefill done
- t0+282ms: decode work item enqueued to long_q (enqueue_ts resets here)
- then it keeps getting popped/put back due to token budget guardrail, which re-enqueues again (enqueue_ts resets AGAIN)

Marcus Reed: so for long items, enqueue_ts is not stable; aging never reaches threshold because it restarts each time we defer.

Benji Okafor: ah, so it’s starvation by “requeue resets age”. are we doing requeue on budget overrun and also on kernel selection mismatch?

Marcus Reed: both. budget overrun is main driver in this repro. kernel mismatch shows up but less frequent.

Yuki Sato: kernel mismatch requeue is expected but we should avoid it thrashing. if it’s causing extra requeues it would amplify this.

Lena Fischer: ok. proposal: aging should be based on a monotonic “first_seen_ts” (or “queue_entry_ts” that doesn’t reset on requeue), not per-requeue enqueue_ts. we can keep enqueue_ts for latency metrics but use a separate field for starvation.

Marcus Reed: +1. I hacked a quick fix locally: track `req.class_enter_ts[class]` the first time it enters that class queue. don’t reset on requeue. then use that for aging decisions.

Marcus Reed: also think we need a hard guardrail: even if bias says short, enforce `long_min_share` > 0 or “force long every N iters when long_q nonempty”. right now `long_min_share` default is 0, so the system can legitimately choose 100% short forever.

Sofia Ivanova: agree on having a guaranteed progress knob. even a tiny min share protects us from bugs + weird distributions.

Julian Moore: for observability: can we add metric `scheduler.class_age_ms_p95` computed off the stable timestamp so SRE can see it rising?

Marcus Reed: yep. I’ll add alongside existing queue time metrics.

Lena Fischer: can you paste the patch sketch?

Marcus Reed: rough diff (not clean yet):
```
// request.h
struct Request {
  int64_t created_ts_ms;
  int64_t class_enter_ts_ms[2]; // [SHORT, LONG], init=-1
  ...
}

// scheduler.cc
int64_t age_ms(const Request& r, Class c, int64_t now_ms) {
  auto t = r.class_enter_ts_ms[c];
  if (t < 0) t = r.created_ts_ms;
  return now_ms - t;
}

void enqueue(Request* r, Class c) {
  if (r->class_enter_ts_ms[c] < 0) r->class_enter_ts_ms[c] = now_ms();
  q[c].push(r);
}

bool should_force_long() {
  if (q[LONG].empty()) return false;
  if (cfg.long_min_share > 0) return long_dispatched / total_dispatched < cfg.long_min_share;
  // fallback: if any long has age > aging_ms * 4, force
  return p95_age_ms(LONG) > cfg.aging_ms * 4;
}

pick_class() {
  if (should_force_long()) return LONG;
  ... existing bias logic ...
}
```

Omar El-Sayed: careful: `created_ts_ms` includes time spent in prefill, which might be ok for “time in system” fairness, but we might want “time waiting for decode capacity”. class_enter_ts_ms[LONG] seems right.

Lena Fischer: yeah. using class_enter_ts_ms[LONG] for long decode fairness; don’t mix prefill time.

Sofia Ivanova: also, budget overrun requeue shouldn’t reset class_enter_ts_ms. good.

Benji Okafor: where does `p95_age_ms(LONG)` come from? we can’t compute P95 cheaply every iter.

Marcus Reed: yeah, in real code I’d use head-of-queue age or a cheap EWMA. the point is to force long when head age crosses threshold.

Lena Fischer: recommend: use head age (oldest item) since it’s what matters for starvation. `age_ms(q[LONG].front()) > X`.

Julian Moore: re metrics, we can export `head_age_ms{class=...}` and maybe `oldest_age_ms` as a gauge.

Marcus Reed: good call.

grafana-bot: Snapshot created: https://grafana.redwood.ai/s/rtSchedStarve/3h8K2
Panels: queue_depth_by_class, dispatch_share_by_class, time_in_queue_p95, starvation_counter

Yuki Sato: question: does forcing long risk tanking TTFT for short? if we set min share too high.

Lena Fischer: we’ll keep it tiny default (e.g., 2-5%). also only applies when long queue non-empty. it’s a safety valve.

Sofia Ivanova: action items:
1) Marcus: PR for stable aging timestamp + not resetting on requeue
2) Lena: update default knobs proposal (`long_min_share` default > 0?) for review
3) Julian: add metrics `scheduler.class_oldest_age_ms` and `scheduler.forced_dispatch_total{class}`

Marcus Reed: ack. I’ll turn this into a follow-up PR off 24844. aiming today.

Marcus Reed: also will add a regression test: constant short arrivals + one long every 10s, assert max long wait < 5s under default config.

Lena Fischer: please do. we need it in CI before canary.

Sofia Ivanova: +1. ping me on the PR, I’ll review quickly.

Marcus Reed: will do. :thumbsup:
